text: You're just trying to update a tiny app, but the download is massive. Ever wonder why a small bug fix needs a multi-gigabyte update?
Logically, you'd expect only the *changed* bits to be sent, right? Just a quick patch for that one specific tweak.
But software isn't one block; it's a complex, interconnected web of components, each relying on others. Think of it like a house of cards.
When one tiny piece is altered, the entire module often needs rebuilding and repackaging, ensuring stability across the whole system.
So even if only a single line of code was tweaked, the download is a new, complete package of many files, ensuring everything works together seamlessly.
That huge file isn't just the change itself; it's the carefully assembled, verified, and stable structure of your entire application.
